1811: Paraguay declares independence. Paraguay declared independence 'in the same year (14 and 15 May 1811)'.

25 July 1812: the First Republic falls. 'Miranda capitulated to Monteverde and signed an armistice on 25 July 1812' (Venezuelan War of Independence page; independence had been declared 'on 5 July 1811'). Cliopatria's 1812 shape adds 1,705 Venezuelan cells. The earlier entry rested on Cliopatria's year (confidence 1).

region.text: Venezuela, held by the patriots' Second Republic

ledger.note: 6 August 1813: Bolívar's campaign restores the patriot republic. 'Bolívar entered Caracas on 6 August 1813, proclaiming the restoration of the Venezuelan Republic' (Venezuelan War of Independence page). Cliopatria keeps Venezuela Spanish through 1813 and drops it in 1814 (a snapshot of the Second Republic's year, shape 1814), so the page's date is a year before the shape change. The earlier entry (a 1814 'slip', confidence 1) is replaced; the royalist return is the next event.
1814: the royalists retake Chile (the Reconquista). The page says royalists 'controlled from 1814 to 1817'; Rancagua is not named.

region.text: Venezuela, held by the patriots' Second Republic

ledger.note: 1814: the Second Republic falls. Bolívar's forces 'were defeated by Boves in 1814' (the page gives the year only); the royalists hold Venezuela again, and it was 'replaced in 1815 by a formal expedition sent from Spain under the leadership of Pablo Morillo'. Cliopatria's 1814 shape still has Venezuela out and returns it in 1815 (keyframe 1815).

1814: Montevideo falls to the United Provinces. 'On 17 May 1814, Vigodet negotiated the surrender.' The page contradicts itself on the date: infobox 'Fall of Montevideo: 23 June 1814', text 'on 23 May 1814, Carlos María de Alvear ... took over the city'.
1814: Montevideo, the last royalist city of the Río de la Plata, is lost (month uncertain: May or June).

region.text: New Granada and Venezuela, reconquered by Morillo's army

ledger.note: 1815: Morillo's expedition retakes New Granada and Venezuela. 'Spain organized in 1815 the largest armed force it ever sent to the New World'; royalists 'controlled from 1815 to 1819'.

region.text: northern and central Chile (Chiloé stays royalist)

ledger.note: 1817: San Martín takes Chile. 'In January 1817, San Martín was finally ready to advance against the royalists in Chile. By 10 February, he had control of northern and central Chile.' Independence is declared in 1818.
1819: Bolívar takes Bogotá. 'From June to July 1819 ... Bolívar led his army' across the Andes; 'By August Bolívar was in control of Bogotá.'
1821: Carabobo ends Spanish rule in Venezuela. The Gran Colombian forces 'decisively defeated the royalist forces' at Carabobo on 24 June. Cliopatria's Gran Colombia row starts 1822.
1821: San Martín enters Lima. 'On the 12th San Martín entered Lima, where he was declared Protector of the Country on 28 July.' The royalist government retreats to the highlands.

1821: Florida passes to the United States. 'The Adams-Onís Treaty was signed between the United States and Spain on February 22, 1819, and took effect on July 17, 1821'; 'Spanish Florida ceased to exist in 1821'. Spanish Empire page: 'Spain gave up its claims in the West of North America in the Adams-Onis Treaty of 1819'.
1821: Central America declares independence. 'On 15 September 1821, an Act of Independence was signed in Guatemala City.'

region.text: New Spain: Mexico and the northern borderlands

ledger.note: 1821: New Spain ends. 'Declaration of Independence: 28 September 1821'; 'The resulting Treaty of Córdoba, which was signed on 24 August' (Wars of independence page); 'At its conclusion in 1821, the viceroyalty was dissolved and the Mexican Empire was established.' Cliopatria's First Mexican Empire row begins 1822.
1821: Santo Domingo proclaims independence. 'finally decided to overthrow the Spanish government and proclaimed the independence of' ... (December 1, 1821); Haiti invades on 9 February 1822.
1822: Pichincha frees Quito. Sucre's forces 'finally conquered Quito' on 24 May 1822.
1824: Ayacucho ends Spanish rule in Peru. Bolívar and Sucre 'destroyed a royalist army under La Serna's command in the Battle of Ayacucho on 9 December 1824'.

region.text: the fortress of San Juan de Ulúa at Veracruz

ledger.note: 1825: the Veracruz fortress falls (the page gives only 'until 1825-1826'): 'Spanish fortifications in Veracruz, Callao and Chiloé resisted until 1825-1826'.
1825: the last royalists of Upper Peru surrender. 'Olañeta died at Tumusla, and his royalist troops surrendered' on 2 April; 'Sucre proclaimed Upper Peru's independence' on 6 August.
1826: Callao falls (the page gives only 'until 1825-1826').

1826: Chiloé falls, the last Spanish land on the American mainland-side islands (the page gives only 'until 1825-1826'); 'Only Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Spanish Virgin Islands and, briefly, Santo Domingo remained under Spanish rule.'

1860: Morocco cedes Sidi Ifni. 'ceded Sidi Ifni to Spain as a part of the Treaty of Tangiers'; Cliopatria's 1861 shape adds 4 Moroccan cells. [Repair 2026-10-19: the Hispano-Moroccan War page does not use the name 'Treaty of Tangiers'; it dates the Treaty of Wad-Ras (Peace of Tétouan) to 26 April 1860 and describes the retrocession of Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequeña, 'a territory of uncertain location by that time, ultimately Ifni', without a date for the cession; the year 1860 is kept at confidence 2 and no month is given.]
1861: Spain annexes the Dominican Republic. 'In March 1861, Santana officially restored the Dominican Republic to Spain.'
1863: the Restoration War begins. 'On August 16, 1863, fourteen Dominican dissidents led by Santiago Rodríguez crossed the northeastern border'.

region.text: the Chincha Islands (30 km round Pisco)

ledger.note: 14 April 1864: the Spanish fleet seizes the Chincha Islands. 'On April 14, 1864, in retaliation for Peru's refusal to pay an indemnity, the Spanish fleet seized the lightly defended' Chincha Islands and occupied them with 400 marines. The islands are approximated by a 30 km radius round the port of Pisco, the nearest mainland place in the gazetteer (the gazetteer lacks the Chincha Islands).
1865: Spain gives up. 'in March 1865, Queen Isabella annulled the annexation'; 'the last Spanish troops departing by July' (infobox 'July 11, 1865').
1865: Spain leaves Santo Domingo for good: 'the last Spanish troops departing by July' (infobox 'July 11, 1865'). Cliopatria keeps the 242 Dominican cells in the Spanish shape to 1872.

region.text: the Chincha Islands (30 km round Pisco)

ledger.note: 1866: the Spanish fleet leaves the islands. After the battle of Callao (2 May 1866) it 'vacated the Chincha Islands' and returned to Spain by the Philippines; the page gives no day. Peru declared war about 14 January 1866, Valparaíso was shelled on 31 March 1866.

1868: the Ten Years' War begins in Cuba. 'In Cuba, the First War for Independence was fought from 1868 to 1878.' The page gives the span and no front; the whole island is the researcher's reading (the rebels held the east).

region.text: the Philippine part of the Sultanate of Sulu (Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, Basilan), as Cliopatria draws it in 1877

ledger.note: February 1876: Malcampo's fleet and army take Jolo. the fleet anchored on February 20 and 'The army advanced at daylight on the 29th, the fleet opening upon the forts at the same time' (Spanish-Moro conflict page; the page gives no month for the 29th, February 1876 by the sequence). Spain had taken Jolo in 1851 and the sultan recognised Spanish sovereignty in a treaty of 19 April 1851 (page; the Sultanate of Sulu page has 30 April 1851 and says the sultan took it for a treaty between equals), but the sultanate went on as an independent state (Cliopatria's Sultanate of Sulu row runs to 1879).
1878: the Ten Years' War ends; Cuba stays Spanish. 'the First War for Independence was fought from 1868 to 1878'.

region.text: the Philippine part of the Sultanate of Sulu (Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, Basilan), as Cliopatria draws it in 1877

ledger.note: 22 July 1878: the Treaty of Licup. The page quotes 'the treaty of the Sultan of Jolo and his datus submitting to Spain, signed at Licup (Jolo) July 22, 1878' and says it established Spanish sovereignty over the Sulu Archipelago; the Sultanate of Sulu page: the sultanate was destroyed in 1878 'with a formal surrender and capitulation', and moved its capital to Maimbung.

region.text: the Philippine part of the Sultanate of Sulu (Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, Basilan), as Cliopatria draws it in 1877

ledger.note: 22 July 1878: Sulu submits to Spain by the Treaty of Licup. Drawn as a vassal (lighter tint), not as annexed land: the Sultanate of Sulu page's infobox dates a Spanish protectorate 1851-1899 and the Spanish East Indies page says the rest of Mindanao was 'nominally under Spanish control... left to administer their own affairs'. The relation lasts to the end of this dossier (the Spanish-American War, the Sultanate of Sulu page: Spain left 'as a consequence of their defeat'); Cliopatria's Sulu row runs to 1879 and overlaps this land 1878-1879.
1895: the Second War of Independence begins in Cuba. 'The Second War for Independence occurred between 1895 and 1898.'

region.text: Luzon, where the revolution began in Central Luzon and Cavite

ledger.note: August 1896: the revolution begins. The Philippine government endorses 'initially August 26 in Balintawak, and later August 23 in Pugad Lawin'; Bonifacio's attack on Manila came on 29-30 August 1896 and the fighting 'initially flared up in Central Luzon' and spread to the Southern Tagalog region, 'particularly in Cavite province' (Philippine Revolution page). The counterpart has no dossier yet (the Katipunan, later the First Philippine Republic).

region.text: Luzon, where the revolution began in Central Luzon and Cavite

ledger.note: 14-15 December 1897: the Pact of Biak-na-Bato ends the first phase ('on December 14 to 15, 1897, the Pact of Biak-na-Bato was signed'); Aguinaldo and the other leaders left for exile in Hong Kong on 24 December 1897.

region.text: Luzon, where the revolution began in Central Luzon and Cavite

ledger.note: 19 May 1898: Aguinaldo returns and resumes the attacks ('On May 19, Aguinaldo, unofficially allied with the United States, returned to the Philippines and resumed attacks against the Spaniards'); the independence declaration of 12 June 1898 was recognised by neither Spain nor the United States; 'By June 1898, the island of Luzon, except for Manila and the port of Cavite, was under Filipino control.'
1898: the war ends in the Treaty of Paris. 'the formal peace treaty, the Treaty of Paris, was signed in Paris on December 10, 1898'; hostilities had halted on 12 August 1898.

region.text: Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines

ledger.note: 1898: Spain cedes Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines to the United States. The treaty 'ceded ownership of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines to the U.S.'; the Philippines cession carried '$20 million'; East Indies page: 'United States annexation of the Philippines and Guam: 10 December 1898'.

1898: Spain gives up Cuba. 'Spain relinquishes sovereignty over Cuba effectively recognizing US occupation'; the US military government dates from 17 July 1898 and independence from 20 May 1902; the treaty 'came into force in Cuba on April 11, 1899'. fx-48 (3 Nov 2026), mirror of captaincy-general-of-cuba/ledger/14: the counterpart was united-states-of-america, which drew Cuba as US land (and then as occupied by the not-yet-born Republic of Cuba). Treaty of Paris page: 'Spain relinquished all claims of sovereignty over and title to Cuba.' and 'Upon Spain's departure, Cuba was to be occupied by the United States'; signed 10 December 1898, in force 11 April 1899. Cuba is not ceded, so the cells go to nobody and united-states-of-america/ledger/83 records the occupation.

region.text: Luzon, where the revolution began in Central Luzon and Cavite

ledger.note: 10 December 1898: the Treaty of Paris ends Spanish rule in the Philippines (see the loss to the United States below). The Philippine Revolution page gives no date for the treaty; the Philippine-American War begins in February 1899.

region.text: the Carolines, Palau and the Northern Marianas (Guam excepted)

ledger.note: 12 February 1899: Spain sells its remaining Pacific islands to Germany. 'Francisco Silvela signed the treaty on 12 February 1899'; 'It transferred the Caroline Islands and the Northern Mariana Islands to Germany'; Palau, 'at the time considered part of the Carolines'; Guam was excluded (the United States took it in 1898); price 25 million pesetas. The page does not say when the transfer took effect (a royal decree of 13 June 1899, publication in the Gaceta on 1 July 1899). The Spanish East Indies page: 'Sale of the remaining islands to Germany: 12 February 1899'. The Marianas are '(1667-1898 or 1899)', the Carolines '(1686-1899)' and Palau '(1574-1899)' there.

February 1899: the overseas empire of the Americas, Asia and the Pacific ends; the African posts remain. Cuba, Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines were lost on 10 December 1898 (Treaty of Paris, see the two December events) and the Pacific islands were sold to Germany on 12 February 1899 (German-Spanish Treaty page); the Spanish Empire page says Spain 'then sold its remaining Pacific Ocean possessions to Germany in the German–Spanish Treaty', keeping only its African territories, and dates the whole empire 'between 1492 and 1976'. This dossier follows Cliopatria's Spanish Empire row, a colonial empire, and ends it here: Fernando Pó and Annobón (gained 1778) and Ifni (1860) pass to the Kingdom of Spain (the page: Spanish Guinea 1926 to 1959, Ifni returned to Morocco in 1969, Spanish Sahara withdrawn 1976). Replaces the former dissolve of December 1898, which gave the Pacific islands to the United States against its own note.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire
wars.outcome: Spanish victory: Tenochtitlan falls on 13 August 1521 and the Kingdom of New Spain is established on 18 August 1521.
wars.note: 'Conquest of the Aztec Empire: 1519-21' (Spanish Empire page).

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire
wars.outcome: Spanish victory: Cuzco and Quito held by 1534, Lima founded 1535; the last Inca stronghold falls in 1572.
wars.note: Cajamarca 1532; 'The last Inca stronghold was conquered by the Spanish in 1572'.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Maya
wars.outcome: Spanish victory; the Itza of the Petén are the last, in 1697.
wars.note: 'Conquest of the Maya: 1524-1697'; no finer dates on the pages opened.

wars.name: Chichimeca War
wars.outcome: Peace made by the crown in 1591; the silver towns of Zacatecas and Guanajuato (founded 1548) are secured.
wars.note: 'the crown ended the long-running Chichimeca War by making peace' (1591); the colonization page has 'a 50-year war (ca. 1550-1600)'.

wars.name: War of the Portuguese Succession
wars.outcome: Philip II recognized as king of Portugal by the Cortes of Tomar in 1581; the Portuguese empire stays under Portuguese administration.
wars.note: War began 25 August 1580; 'Spain conquered Portugal and the Azores Islands from 1580 to 1582' (Spanish Empire page). No Spanish Empire land changes hands; the union tint is in the ledger.

wars.name: Destruction of the Seven Cities (Mapuche uprising)
wars.outcome: The Mapuche reverse colonization south of the Bío-Bío.
wars.note: 'the Mapuche successfully reversed colonization with the Destruction of the Seven Cities in 1599-1604'.

wars.name: Dutch conquest of Spanish Formosa
wars.outcome: Dutch victory: 'Loss of Spanish Formosa to the Dutch: 26 August 1642'.
wars.note: A sidebar of the page says Spain held Formosa 'from 1575 until the Dutch invasion in 1646', against 1626-1642 elsewhere.

wars.name: English conquest of Jamaica
wars.outcome: Jamaica lost to England.
wars.note: The page gives 'Jamaica (1655)' as an English colony only; the war is not narrated on the pages opened.

wars.name: Pueblo Revolt
wars.outcome: The Spanish are expelled in 1680 and return in 1692.
wars.note: 'The unrest led to the Pueblo Revolt in 1680, expelling the Spanish, who retreated to Paso del Norte'; 'After the return of the Spanish in 1692'.

wars.name: Carolina and Creek raids on the Spanish missions
wars.outcome: The mission frontier of Georgia and northern Florida is destroyed; St. Augustine and the peninsula stay Spanish.
wars.note: 'The missions were destroyed by Carolina and Creek raiders in a series of raids from 1702 to 1704'. The page does not name the war.

wars.name: Guaraní War
wars.outcome: The Guaraní are defeated (Caiboaté, 10 February 1756) and driven from the seven missions ceded to Portugal; the Treaty of El Pardo (1761) annuls the exchange.
wars.note: Armistice at the end of 1754; the Portuguese held the missions 'until 1759 when Spain unilaterally ended the Treaty of Madrid' (the page also says El Pardo, 1761).

wars.name: Seven Years' War (British capture of Manila and Havana)
wars.outcome: Manila (October 1762 to April 1764) and Havana occupied; returned under the 1763 Treaty of Paris, which also cedes Florida to Britain (10 February 1763) while Spain gains Louisiana (23 November 1762).
wars.note: 'In October 1762, a British expeditionary force captured Manila'; 'all British-occupied territories in the Spanish East Indies were returned to Spain'.

wars.name: Anglo-Spanish War (1779-1783)
wars.outcome: Spain takes West Florida (Baton Rouge, Natchez, Mobile, Pensacola) and regains East Florida in the Peace of Paris of 1783.
wars.note: The war's name is not on the page; 'declared war on Great Britain on May 8, 1779'.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of the Misiones Orientales
wars.outcome: Portugal takes the Misiones Orientales; confirmed by the Treaty of Badajoz (1801).
wars.note: 'From 1801 to 1802 ... captured by Portuguese forces and discontented Guaraní people'.

wars.name: Reconquista of Santo Domingo
wars.outcome: Spanish victory: Palo Hincado (7 November 1808), French capitulation 9 July 1809.
wars.note: Followed by 'a twelve-year period of Spanish rule'.

wars.name: Spanish American wars of independence

zones.text: the mainland that Cliopatria's Spanish row loses between 1811 and 1824, front by front in the ledger

wars.outcome: Spain loses the mainland by 1825-1826 (Ayacucho 9 December 1824, Callao and Chiloé 1826); 'Only Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Spanish Virgin Islands and, briefly, Santo Domingo remained under Spanish rule.'
wars.note: The page's lead lists the 1829 Battle of Tampico (Barradas's attempt to reconquer Mexico) as the closing action; Spain did not recognize Mexico until 1836.

wars.name: Dominican Restoration War
wars.outcome: Spain withdraws: annexation annulled in March 1865, last troops gone by July (infobox 'July 11, 1865').
wars.note: Began 16 August 1863.

wars.name: Ten Years' War
wars.outcome: Cuba stays Spanish.
wars.note: 'In Cuba, the First War for Independence was fought from 1868 to 1878'; the rebel state needs a dossier (type rebel).

wars.name: Cuban War of Independence
wars.outcome: Merges into the Spanish-American War.
wars.note: 'The Second War for Independence occurred between 1895 and 1898.'

wars.name: Spanish-American War
wars.outcome: Protocol of peace 12 August 1898; Treaty of Paris signed 10 December 1898: Spain relinquishes Cuba and cedes Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.
wars.note: War declared by the United States on 25 April 1898 (the page also says a state of war had existed since 21 April).

wars.name: Fantastic War

zones.text: Rio Grande de Sao Pedro (Vila do Rio Grande) and its bar

wars.outcome: Spanish capture of Colonia del Sacramento (11 October 1762) and Rio Grande de São Pedro; the Treaty of Paris (1763) restores the status quo; Colonia returns on 27 December 1763.
wars.note: The page says Spain would lose all conquests except the forts of Santa Teresa and San Miguel; the 1776-1777 war page has Rio Grande held until 1776 and is followed.

wars.name: Spanish–Portuguese War (1776–1777)

zones.text: Rio Grande de Sao Pedro (Vila do Rio Grande) and its bar

wars.outcome: Portugal retakes Rio Grande in February 1776; Cevallos takes Santa Catarina island (23 February 1777) and Colonia (3 June 1777); the First Treaty of San Ildefonso (1 October 1777) returns the island and gives Colonia to Spain.
wars.note: The Río de la Plata page used elsewhere has Colonia surrendering on 4 June; this page has 'The town capitulated on June 3'.

wars.name: Hispano-Moroccan War (1859–1860)
wars.outcome: Spanish victory: Tétouan entered 6 February 1860, Treaty of Wad-Ras (26 April 1860) with an indemnity, Spanish administration of Tétouan until it was paid, and the retrocession of Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequeña ('ultimately Ifni').
wars.note: A declaration of war was passed by the Congress of Deputies on 22 October 1859. The page does not call the treaty 'Tangiers' and gives no date for the Ifni cession; no contest zone is drawn (the occupied Tétouan area is not in the Spanish shape).

wars.name: Chincha Islands War
wars.outcome: Spain seizes the Chincha Islands (14 April 1864), shells Valparaíso (31 March 1866), fights the battle of Callao (2 May 1866), then leaves the islands; peace with Peru 1879, Bolivia 1879, Ecuador 1885, Chile 1883, an indefinite armistice in 1871.
wars.note: Peru declared war about 14 January 1866, Ecuador on 30 January and Bolivia on 22 March 1866.

wars.name: Spanish–Moro conflict

zones.text: the Philippine part of the Sultanate of Sulu (Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, Basilan), as Cliopatria draws it in 1877

wars.outcome: Jolo falls to Malcampo's expedition in February 1876; the sultan and his datus submit by the Treaty of Licup (22 July 1878).
wars.note: The article covers 1565-1898 (Balanguingui 1848, Jolo 1851, Maguindanao 1862 and 1887); only the 1876-1878 Sulu campaign changes this ledger.

wars.name: Philippine Revolution

zones.text: Luzon, where the revolution began in Central Luzon and Cavite

wars.outcome: The revolution begins in August 1896, pauses with the Pact of Biak-na-Bato (14-15 December 1897), resumes on 19 May 1898 and by June 1898 holds Luzon except Manila and Cavite; Spain cedes the Philippines by the Treaty of Paris.
wars.note: The counterpart has no dossier (Katipunan, then the First Philippine Republic proclaimed 12 June 1898).

certainty.note: Claims along the Tordesillas line, mission frontiers and the Amazon are approximate; the Caribbean and Philippine coasts are islands.
Sharper lines: Colonia and the Misiones Orientales (San Ildefonso 1777, undone 1801), the 31st parallel (Pinckney 1795) and the Adams-Onís line (1819); the interior of South America stays soft.

The coasts of the island colonies (Cuba, Puerto Rico, Guam) are sharp, but the Philippines are soft: the Spanish East Indies page says the highlands of Luzon stayed outside Spanish control until the early 19th century, Mindanao was 'nominally under Spanish control... left to administer their own affairs' and southern Palawan was reached only in the late 1890s; Sulu was taken in 1876-1878 and overlaps the Sultanate of Sulu row to 1879. Ends with the Treaty of Paris (10 December 1898).
The Pacific islands sold by treaty on 12 February 1899 and the African posts, whose coasts are the shapes.

notes:
Written by am-06-b from 14 Wikipedia pages opened with WebFetch on 2026-10-19 (the page budget; one more URL failed, see below), then repaired the same day after the review with 22 more pages (REPAIR 2026-10-19 below). Every shape cites a page; in shapes 1572, 1659 and 1670 (and the Amazon block of 1778) a block of cells could not be checked within the budget and the note says 'unverified: page budget'. Many shape changes are dated by the pages only to the year or the span, so the evidence for a keyframe is usually 'the page gives the event, and Cliopatria's shape year matches it within a year'. After the repair the events at confidence 1 are the Treaty of Madrid block (1750); the earlier seven (Michoacán 1534, Yucatán 1547, Havana 1762 and 1763, Trinidad 1797, Venezuela 1812 and 1814) now rest on pages.

ONE ROW, NOT TWO: Cliopatria's rel-spanish-empire is an umbrella (1516..1931) and is not a state. The state is the 'Spanish Empire' row; the Kingdom of Spain row (1516..2024, the peninsula) and the First Spanish Republic row (1873..1876, one shape that holds Spain, Cuba and the Philippines) are separate rows to be handled by the dossier owners of those slugs. This dossier ends the colonial empire in February 1899 (Treaty of Paris signed 10 December 1898, Pacific islands sold on 12 February 1899) though Cliopatria's row ends in 1879; the colonies from 1873 to 1899 are described in the new keyframes spanish-empire_1873, _1878 and _1899 and they overlap the First Spanish Republic and Kingdom of Spain rows (the owner of those slugs should drop the colonies from them, or the renderer should let this dossier win).

THE THIN ENDING: Cliopatria's shape 1877 has one cell and is marked wrong; the 1865 and 1873 keyframes replace Cliopatria's colonies-only shapes 1853..1879 with the Dominican Republic removed (1865) and the Pacific islands added (1873, Guam, Northern Marianas, Carolines, Palau; the page gives Spain holding them to 1899).

PORTUGUESE LANDS 1582-1639: Cliopatria's Spanish Empire shapes 1582-1639 hold the Portuguese overseas lands (Brazil, Angola, Mozambique, Goa, Malacca and the rest). The Iberian Union page says the empires stayed separately administered. Every shape 1582..1636 carries an 'adjust' verdict whose geometry is unchanged and whose text says the Portuguese lands are a personal-union tint, and the ledger records them as vassal_start 1581 and vassal_end 1640 with counterpart portuguese-empire (portuguese-empire records the same two dates as a loss in 1581 and a gain in 1640-12: the dates agree, the event type does not; the Iberian Union page supports the vassal reading, and the orchestrator must align the two dossiers). The renderer should draw the tint, not Spanish rule. The country list used to build the tint (PORT_COUNTRIES) is the researcher's reading of the 1595 shape and may omit small enclaves; nothing in the dossier removes cells.

LOUISIANA IS MISSING FROM CLIOPATRIA: the Spanish Empire row has no Louisiana at any date. The Louisiana (New Spain) page says France transferred Louisiana on 23 November 1762 and the transfer back to France took place on 30 November 1803 (the date Spain 'lost' it de facto; San Ildefonso 1800 is the de jure retrocession). Shapes 1762-1803 are 'adjust' with the gazetteer region 'Louisiana' added (about 10,200 cells). The French-Louisiana row (slug french-louisiana) should end 1762 and resume 1803 in its dossier; this dossier names it as the counterpart of the 1803 loss and new-france for 1762. The gazetteer region 'Louisiana' is the Louisiana Purchase by whole states and overshoots (its own note: Montana, Wyoming and Colorado are whole states, Minnesota east of the Mississippi is not included), so the added area is larger than the 2.28 million km2 that the page gives for the colony; the gazetteer agent may refine it.

WEST FLORIDA AND THE FLORIDAS: the Cliopatria shape drops Spanish Florida in 1763 and 1702-1708 is misdated (the missions fell 1702-1704; the shape drops Florida 1702 to 1708). West Florida (Baton Rouge, Natchez, Mobile, Pensacola) is added in 1779-1781 by war and in 1783 by treaty; Natchez and the Mississippi/Alabama strip north of 31 N is left in the Spanish shape until the Pinckney Treaty (1795) by the keyframes 1783..1794. Adams-Onís: signed 22 February 1819, in force 17 July 1821 (Spanish Florida page). The pages opened give no western boundary line, so the 1819 line in the west is not drawn and the Texas and California edges stay as Cliopatria draws them.

THE MISIONES ORIENTALES (Rio Grande do Sul): Cliopatria keeps the seven missions in the Spanish shape from 1757 to 1810. The Guaraní War page: Treaty of Madrid 1750 gave them to Portugal, the war ran 1754-1756 (Caiboaté, 10 February 1756), and Spain ended the treaty (the page says 1759 in one place and El Pardo in 1761 in another). San Ildefonso (1 October 1777) returned them; Portuguese forces took them in 1801-1802 (Río de la Plata page), so the Cliopatria shape still holds them to 1810. Keyframes 1801-1805 give the corrected shape; the 1801 loss has the Rio Grande do Sul intersect.

PERU AND UPPER PERU: the Cliopatria shapes of 1822 and 1824 remove the Peruvian highlands and Upper Peru early. The Independence page: Lima entered 12 July 1821, but Ayacucho (9 December 1824) and Tumusla (2 April 1825) end the royalist hold. Keyframes 1822 and 1824 correct this. Veracruz, Callao and Chiloé, which 'resisted until 1825-1826' (the page gives no finer dates; the ledger puts Veracruz in 1825, Callao and Chiloé in 1826 as confidence 2), are an enclaves keyframe (1825-1826). The Cliopatria shape 1853 and its later spans are the island colonies only. The mainland leftovers Cliopatria keeps to 1852 are removed by the keyframe 1827.

CHILE 1810-1820: the Independence page has the juntas of 1810, royalists in control 1814-1817 and San Martín in control of northern and central Chile by 10 February 1817. Cliopatria's shape drops central Chile in 1812 (moved to 1810 here), restores it in 1814 (confirmed by the page) and drops it in 1820 (moved to 1817 here). The cell sets are Cliopatria's own differences intersected with the gazetteer's country Chile, because the page names fronts, not borders. South of the Bío-Bío the Mapuche kept their land; the ledger records the 1599 loss (page: 'Destruction of the Seven Cities in 1599-1604') and the Araucanía counterpart needs a dossier.

NEW SPAIN CLAIM VS CONTROL: the Spanish Empire infobox gives 13.7 million km2 for 1780, the Cliopatria shape 1780 holds 11.0 million km2 (Louisiana and the Floridas missing); the New Spain page gives 7.66 million km2 (1790) but Cliopatria's Mexico, Central America and borderlands cells hold about 2.4 million km2 (ratio 0.32), because the page counts the Spanish claim to the interior (Texas to California, the north) and Cliopatria draws the area under control. This dossier leaves the northern frontier as Cliopatria draws it and records the Pueblo Revolt (1680-1692), the California missions (1769) and the Jesuit expulsion (1767, Paraguay reducciones) as events; the Tordesillas line, the Amazon and the Chaco frontier are in the soft certainty band.

DATES THAT DISAGREE BETWEEN PAGES: Formosa fell on 26 August 1642 (East Indies page) but a sidebar of the same page says Spain held it 'from 1575 until the Dutch invasion in 1646'; the 1642 date is used. The Spanish Empire page lists 'Jamaica (1655)' as an English colony and Cliopatria keeps both Jamaica and Taiwan in the Spanish shape to 1658 (new keyframes 1642 and 1655 take them out). The Spanish Empire page gives the Cuban wars as 1868-1878 and 1895-1898. Santo Domingo: Basel 1795, French rule from 1801 (Toussaint), Palo Hincado 7 November 1808, French capitulation 9 July 1809, independence proclaimed 1 December 1821 (Haiti invades 9 February 1822), annexation 18 March 1861 to July 1865; Cliopatria keeps the Spanish shape on Hispaniola until 1872.

STATES THAT NEED A DOSSIER OF THEIR OWN (counterparts used here): the rebel state Republic of Cuba in Arms (1868-1878) and cuban-nationalists (1895-1899) for Cuba; the Mapuche (Araucanía) and the Muisca Confederation as native states; Pueblo peoples (Pueblo Revolt); the Chichimeca peoples (war 1550-1591); Central America (Act of Independence), federal Provinces; and the Jesuit reducciones (slug jesuit-reducciones exists; its owner should take 1609..1767 and the Guaraní War).
